Hi Alex / Priya —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps to qualify Acme for a Private/VPC deployment with our performance SLOs: 

Summary of target SLOs you mentioned on the call:
- End-to-end p95 latency (user request -> first token stream): <= 150 ms
- Sustained throughput target: 500 req/s (payloads with ~256 token outputs)
- Concurrent active sessions: 100 (burst to 300 for short windows)
- Streaming requirement: sub-50ms token interval for real-time streams once started

Key VPC/network questions we need to validate to confirm the SLOs can be met in your environment:
1) Network path: Are you planning VPC peering, AWS Transit Gateway, or VPN (IPsec) between Acme app VPCs and Redwood private subnet?
2) Egress/NAT: Will outbound NATting be required from Redwood instances, or can we use static egress IPs via NAT Gateway or a customer-managed firewall?
3) MTU and fragmentation: Do you have any non-standard MTU settings across peered connections?
4) Expected internal latency budget: can you share typical L3/L4 latency between your app frontends and the target region (us-west-2) or between your AZs (p50/p95)? We're looking for sub-20ms internal hop latencies ideally.
5) Allowed ports / TLS termination: We require outbound 443 (mutual TLS) to our control plane and internal ports for health checks/metrics if you want private peering.

Requested artifacts (if you can upload to the Drive link above or reply to this thread):
- Simple network diagram (VPC IDs, peering/transit layout, NAT/Firewalls) — we referenced acme_vpc_network_diagram.pdf attached.
- Traceroutes from your app-hosts to us (examples: traceroute -w 2 -q 1 <redwood-ip>) and any recent packet loss stats (attached acme_traceroute_jan2026.txt).
- Expected QPS and typical payload sizes (you started this in the call; providing daily/hourly distribution helps us size caching/batching).

Proposed timeline / next steps:
- If you can share the artifacts above, Marissa (CC'd) and our infra team will propose a focused lab test plan (end-to-end test, streaming stress, and controlled added latency) — ETA 2 business days to send test plan once we have traceroutes + network diagram.
- Schedule a 60-minute lab kickoff with your NetOps and App SREs to walk through firewall rules and run an initial traceroute / tcpdump.

I'll also attach a preliminary SLO matrix (slo_matrix_acme.csv) so we can confirm targets and acceptance criteria.

Best,
Jordan Blake

2) Egress/NAT: We currently have NAT Gateways in each AZ; we can reserve a static Elastic IP for the Redwood egress path if needed.

4) Latency: Typical p50 between app frontends and model-serving subnets in us-west-2 is ~6-8ms, p95 ~18-22ms (cross-AZ higher). We will try to provide more detailed samples.
5) Ports/TLS: No problem for outbound 443. For private peering we can open a small set of health/metrics ports — we'll confirm exact ports with Priya.

Hi all —

Thanks — I put together a test plan and network checklist and attached it (redwood_test_plan.pdf) along with an updated SLO matrix (slo_matrix_acme.csv) that maps acceptance criteria to test cases. High-level plan below: 

Test plan (high level):
1) Baseline network validation (Priya runs on-prem / app host): traceroute, mtr to Redwood egress IPs, curl -w '%{time_total} %{time_starttransfer}' against our health endpoint on a small sample of hosts (we provided shell snippets in the attachment). Collect p50/p95 and packet loss.
2) Controlled lab load (run from Redwood infra in their VPC using Transit Gateway): emulate 0, 50, 100, 200 concurrent streams with a k6 script for request-level load (we'll share the k6 script). We'll also run a streaming harness that simulates token-by-token output to measure token-interval latency.
3) Cross-AZ and degraded network tests: we will inject additional latency (20-40ms) and 0.5-1% packet loss in the lab to observe SLO degradation and fallback behavior (KV cache, batching reductions).
4) Post-test report: report with p50/p95 latencies, throughput curves, token-interval CDF, and recommendations (NAT/peering tweaks, TCP keepalive tuning, MTU checks).

Network checklist for Priya (summary):
- Confirm Transit Gateway/peering details (TGW IDs) and provide VPC IDs and CIDR ranges for our firewall rules.
- Reserve a static Elastic IP for Redwood egress or allow list Redwood's set of egress IPs.
- Open outbound 443 to our control plane IPs; if you prefer private peering, open our health/metrics ports (range 9000-9010) between peered subnets.
- Allow ICMP for traceroute and mtr during validation window.
- Provide a small set of test host IPs (app host + SRE jump box) for us to coordinate tcpdump captures.

Attachments: redwood_test_plan.pdf, slo_matrix_acme.csv
